findings.title: Weekly team digest exposes aggregate stats of an unrelated team to dual-team members
findings.description: Members who belong to two teams (a common setup after the April matrix reorg) receive a Monday digest email that shows aggregate session/engagement stats for a third team they are not a member of at all, rather than for either of their actual two teams. Confirmed for two different members (Aleksander: consistently shown 'Formulation' team stats for two consecutive Mondays; Fenna: shown a different wrong team). Single-team members' digests are correct. This surfaces sensitive team-level performance data (session counts, average goals-completed, engagement rate) to people outside that team. In-app team dashboard view is accurate; only the emailed digest is affected.
findings.quote: His Monday digest showed him the aggregate stats — session counts, average goals-completed, engagement rate — for a team he is not on.
findings.severity_reason: Wrong/sensitive aggregate performance data (another team's stats) is being exposed to unauthorized members via email, raising data-visibility and compliance concerns for the customer's legal team; a manual workaround (disabling the digest) exists, keeping it below critical.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue covers digest/team-membership data resolving to the wrong team; distinct from PROJ-101 (timezone display) which is a formatting issue, not a data-exposure issue.

findings.title: N/A - workaround request for digest data-exposure bug
findings.description: Customer asks what to do in the interim about the wrong-team digest issue and whether digests can be disabled for affected members. This is a stopgap for the digest bug already logged, not a separate defect.
findings.quote: Is there anything I do in the meantime? Do I tell dual-team people to ignore the digest?
findings.severity_reason: Not a distinct defect; purely a request for interim mitigation guidance tied to the digest data-exposure bug.
findings.match_note: Workaround/stopgap for the same digest team-data-exposure issue at L24; not filed separately.

findings.title: N/A - Boston coach-matching delay attributed to member preference, not product
findings.description: Some Boston members were matched to a coach later than Basel members. Customer explains this was because those specific members held out for a coach with a life-sciences background rather than accepting the first match, and explicitly says 'that's on them, not you.' No product defect identified.
findings.quote: A couple of them were picky about wanting a coach with a life-sciences background specifically, so they held out for the right match rather than taking the first offer.
findings.severity_reason: Explicitly attributed by the customer to member preference/behavior rather than a product or process defect.
findings.match_note: No catalogue entry applies; customer herself rules out a product cause for the delay.
